summary: Describes the SIP PUBLISH extension for publishing event state used within the SIP Events framework. Its first use is publishing presence information, but it can support other kinds of event state too.

eli5.summary: It is how you tell a service your own news, such as that you are free to chat, so it can tell your friends.

questions: how does sip presence publication work
what is an event state compositor
subtitle: The SIP PUBLISH method: how a device tells a server its current presence or other event state.

tldr.problem: The SIP Events framework lets people subscribe to state such as presence, but there was no standard way for the user's own devices to supply that state to the server that distributes it.
tldr.mechanism: A new PUBLISH method carries event state to an Event State Compositor. The server hands back an entity-tag for each publication, and the client quotes it in SIP-If-Match to refresh, modify or remove that state. Published state expires unless refreshed.
tldr.outcome: Several devices can each publish their own state, and the server composites it for subscribers. The first use is presence. The RFC is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 8996.

today: RFC 3903 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 8996. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Publishing Event State
sections.content:
This RFC gives a framework for publishing event state from a user agent to an entity that composites it and passes it to interested parties through the SIP Events framework (RFC 3265). It also defines a concrete use: a presence user agent publishing presence state (RFC 3856) to a presence compositor.

The mechanism can carry any event state for which an event package exists. The RFC gives the example of collecting the statuses of voice-mail boxes across several user agents. It is explicitly not a general-purpose mechanism for carrying arbitrary data, because better-suited mechanisms exist for that.
sections.eli5: Before this, you could look at the whiteboard but there was no agreed way to write on it. PUBLISH is the pen.

sections.title: Key Roles and Terms
sections.content:
The RFC introduces a few terms:

  • Event Publication Agent (EPA): the user agent client that sends PUBLISH requests. For presence this is the presence user agent (PUA).
  • Event State Compositor (ESC): the user agent server that processes them and composites the event state of a resource into a complete composite state. For presence this is the presence agent (PA).
  • Event soft state: state published with PUBLISH. It is identified by an entity-tag and has a defined lifetime, so it expires after a negotiated time.
  • Event hard state: the steady-state or default state the ESC may use in addition to, or without, soft state. Setting it is out of scope.
sections.eli5: The publisher is the person writing on the whiteboard, and the compositor is the teacher keeping it tidy. Soft state is a note in chalk that fades unless you rewrite it; hard state is what is painted on permanently.

sections.title: How Publication Works
sections.content:
PUBLISH is like REGISTER in that it creates, modifies and removes state in another entity on the user's behalf. It is addressed the same way as SUBSCRIBE: the Request-URI names the resource whose state is published. A user may have several endpoints, each publishing its own state, and the ESC builds the composite from them. Through a subscription to the event package, the user can discover the composite state.

The body of a PUBLISH carries the state. For every successful request the ESC assigns an entity-tag, which the EPA uses in later requests to refresh, modify or remove that publication. When state expires or is removed, its entity-tag becomes invalid, and a request using it fails. The EPA must then start again without an entity-tag.

Entity-tags are adapted from HTTP/1.1. In PUBLISH they are a plain token, a precondition applies to a single tag only, there is no special wildcard value, and the ESC must always return one on success. They are opaque to the EPA, which may not infer any structure from them.
sections.eli5: When you write your line on the whiteboard, the teacher gives you a ticket number. You show the ticket every time you want to change, extend or wipe your line.

sections.title: The Four Publication Operations
sections.content:
Which operation a request performs depends on whether it has a body, whether it has a SIP-If-Match header, and its Expires value.

  • Initial: a body, no SIP-If-Match. It sets this EPA's state and leaves state from other EPAs untouched.
  • Refresh: no body, SIP-If-Match present. It only extends the lifetime, so it MUST NOT have a body.
  • Modify: a body and SIP-If-Match. The old state is replaced by the new.
  • Remove: no body, SIP-If-Match present, and Expires: 0.

An EPA MUST NOT send a new PUBLISH for the same Request-URI until it has a final response or the earlier request has timed out. Each 2xx response carries a fresh SIP-ETag that the EPA MUST store in place of the old one. The Expires header suggests a lifetime. The ESC may lower it but never extend it, and the 2xx response says the actual duration.
sections.eli5: You can write a new line, say 'keep my line a bit longer', change what it says, or erase it. Each of these is a slightly different request with your ticket.

sections.title: How the Compositor Processes a PUBLISH
sections.content:
The ESC processes requests for the same Request-URI in the order received, and atomically: each is processed completely or not at all. Beyond normal UAS rules, it follows these steps.

  1. If the Request-URI is not a resource it maintains, return 404.
  2. If the Event header is missing or names an unsupported package, return 489.
  3. With no SIP-If-Match, generate and store a locally unique entity-tag. If the header holds more than one tag, return 400. If the tag matches nothing, return 412.
  4. Take the requested expiration from Expires or a local default. The ESC may choose less, and may reject too-short intervals with 423 carrying Min-Expires.
  5. Check the content type (415 if it does not match), then store, refresh or remove the state. An expiry of 0 removes it immediately. Internal errors fail the request, for example with 504.
  6. Return 200 with an Expires header and a new SIP-ETag, different from any tag previously assigned for that Request-URI.

On the client side, a 412 means the EPA MUST NOT retry. It discards that tag and SHOULD perform an initial publication. A 423 may be retried with an Expires at least as large as the Min-Expires.
sections.eli5: The teacher checks the ticket, decides how long the chalk note lasts, writes it down, and gives you a new ticket. If the ticket is no good, you start over.

sections.title: Using PUBLISH in Event Packages
sections.content:
Any event package that uses PUBLISH SHOULD discuss several issues. It must define the content types allowed in publication bodies and prescribe a default, mandatory-to-implement MIME type, and say what a response body means (usually nothing). It should say whether multiple sources of state are expected, how state can be split into segments, and whether to limit publication rates.

For presence, a PUA MUST support the PIDF format (RFC 3863) and MAY support others. A PUA may publish just a subset of the tuples in the presence document, and how the ESC combines them is local policy. The EPA MUST keep each tuple's id consistent within an entity-tag: a tuple missing from a later publication is treated as removed, and a new id as added.

The RFC also suggests ways to ease load on the ESC: choose a longer minimum expiration, or answer a noisy source with 503 and a Retry-After.
sections.eli5: Each kind of whiteboard needs its own rules about what you may write on it. Presence has them built in.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Event state can be sensitive, so the ESC SHOULD authenticate the EPA and apply authorization policy to all requests. ESCs and EPAs MUST implement Digest authentication, and implementations MUST support Digest with replay protection to counter replayed PUBLISH requests, which could spoof old state. ESCs SHOULD throttle incoming publications and the notifications they cause, since state creation can be used to consume a victim's resources.

Even with authentication, a man-in-the-middle could install, change or remove state. Implementations SHOULD at least integrity-protect the To, From, Event, SIP-If-Match, Route and Expires headers and the body. ESCs MUST implement TLS with mutual and one-way authentication and support the SIPS URI scheme; EPAs SHOULD be able to initiate TLS. S/MIME is optional (MAY) for integrity and encryption. If state is protected end to end, the ESC MUST NOT modify it before sending it to subscribers.
sections.eli5: Anyone could scribble on the whiteboard, so the teacher checks who you are, and the note you hand over is sealed so nobody can alter it on the way.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC registers the PUBLISH method, the response code 412 "Conditional Request Failed", and two header field names, SIP-ETag and SIP-If-Match, neither with a compact form. Section 15 gives a presence walkthrough with a watcher, a presence agent and a PUA, showing an initial publication, a refresh that causes no notification, and a modification that does.
sections.eli5: The new method, the new error number and the two new headers were put on the official list.
